----Petitioners  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Bhanwari Devi W/o Ramdayal, Aged About 45 Years, R/o  Baniyo Ka Baas, Bikampur, P.s. Bajju, Bikaner.
For Respondent(s) : Mr. M.S. Bhati, PP  Ms. Anu Choudhary, for respondent  No.2  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Order 21/04/2023

The instant criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.c. has been filed by the petitioners against the order dated 22.09.2022 passed by the learned Civil Judge & Judicial Magistrate Kolayat, District Bikaner, in Case No.242/2022 whereby the learned trial Court has allowed the compromise for offence under Section 420 IPC and declined to compound the offence under Sections 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC on the basis of compromise between the parties.

entities.text: Civil Judge & Judicial Magistrate Kolayat, District Bikaner
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners submits that the matter has already been compromised between the parties and it is borne out from the compromise that respondent No.2 is not inclined to [2023/RJJD/011427] (2 of 2) [CRLMP-1921/2023] proceed further in the matter.

Counsel has placed reliance on a decision of Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr.
[(2012) 10 SCC 303].

entities.text:

[(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In these circumstances, the FIR lodged by the respondent No.2 against the Sahab Ram vs State Of Rajasthan (2023/Rjjd/011427) on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116969332/
1 petitioner may be quashed.

entities.text: Sahab Ram vs State Of Rajasthan (2023/Rjjd/011427)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the respondent concurs the fact of compromise and submits that in view of the compromise, the respondent No.2 does not want to proceed further in the matter.

In view of compromise arrived at between the parties and applying the ratio in decision of Gian Singh (Supra), I deem it just and proper to invoke inherent powers of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, the present misc. petition is allowed and the order dated 22.09.2022 passed by the court below is quashed to the extent of declining to compound the offence under Sections 467, 468,
471 and 120-B of IPC and the offence under Sections 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC is hereby compounded on the basis of compromise deed and the entire criminal proceedings pursuant to Case No.242/2022 and subsequent proceedings are also quashed and set aside on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.
Stay petition is also decided accordingly.
(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 60-Ishan/-
